anchor: if (typeof topology !== "object" || topology === null) return "client.topology (an object)";
reason: a real wall-clock hang on CI, not a slow survivor, but only there: the mutant makes missingDriverInternal report 'client.topology (an object)' for every client, so the bounded stop's start check refuses each connection with MongoDriverInternalsError. On CI at concurrency 1 it ran to the limit in 2 of 2 runs (341 s on de86cc5, 330 s on main f650960), while the whole store-bound dry run takes 20-30 s there (net 4.8-5.4 s) and the 12 other mutants of its range ended Killed in both runs. Alone it never hangs: Killed in 0.3 s by Stryker (alone, concurrency 1, the shard's limits), by hand in 1-6 s (shuffled file orders, no duration cache, the killing file excluded: 2-10 s every time), and in a Linux container (node 24, 2 CPUs, a three-member replica set: Killed in 5 of 5 runs, the whole Stryker run 17-29 s). The cause of the hang on CI is open (a start that fails on MongoDriverInternalsError may leave a client or its monitoring running so that the stop never ends; a stack trace of it needs a Linux runner that hangs: the report of a node started with --report-on-signal, signalled at the limit). scripts/stryker-timeouts.mjs --rerun runs an unlisted Timeout alone; this one stays listed because it is the only one that ran to the limit on CI in every run, and it is judged by CI's evidence, not by a local one
